title: Cargo Door Structure — Cleat and Intercostal Replacement Repair
abstract: Permanent repair for a cracked or distorted cleat in the cargo door internal structure, by replacement of the cleat and the adjacent intercostal with the door removed from the aircraft.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the internal load path of a cargo door after a cleat has been found cracked or distorted, usually following a ground handling contact or an overload of the latching mechanism.
sections.damage_assessment: Inspect the cleat and the adjacent intercostal by detailed visual inspection with the door lining removed, and by dye penetrant inspection where the visual finding is inconclusive. Measure any distortion against the flatness limit on the repair drawing. A cleat that is cracked at the radius, distorted beyond the flatness limit, or that has an elongated fastener hole, must be replaced; there is no blend or straighten option because the material has been worked. Check the adjacent intercostal at the same time, since a cleat rarely fails on its own. Record which latching station the damage is nearest to, because a repeated finding at the same station points at the latching mechanism rather than at handling.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the door from the aircraft to the applicable procedure and put it on the door trestle. Remove the door lining and the latch shroud at the affected station. Remove the fasteners at the cleat, working from the free edge inwards, and take out the cleat D5230113947598. Remove the adjacent intercostal FA933357-01 where it is also damaged. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the surrounding stringer and skin and report any indication. Offer the replacement cleat and check the fit against the stringer land; local packing is permitted up to the thickness on the drawing. Drill and ream the fastener holes to the existing pattern where the holes are sound and to the first oversize where they are not. Deburr and apply the surface protection of the standard practice. Install the cleat and the intercostal wet with sealant using blind rivets AGS534950-40, and add the reinforcing angle ASH985770-45 where the drawing calls for it at a station that has been repaired before. Refit the latch shroud and the lining, and refit the door to the aircraft.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair has no life limit. Do a detailed visual inspection of the repaired cleat at every heavy check and after any reported ground handling contact with the door. Where a station has been repaired twice, the latching mechanism must be rigged and the latch load measured before the door is returned to service. Report every repair to Aeralis with the station identity, because the fleet distribution of these findings is monitored.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: No crack is allowable in a cleat. Distortion up to 1.5 mm across the flange is acceptable without repair provided no fastener hole is elongated and no crack is present at the radius.
